doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Teaching Benny Powell bass trombone
summary: Raph explains that Benny Powell studied bass trombone with him after Lew Van Haney left for Indiana.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I didn’t know Benny Powell played bass trombone.

Benny studied with me. Lew Van Haney was the second trombone player with the New York Philharmonic. And Benny and two other guys from the Basie band studied with Lew. And Van Haney moved out to Indiana to take a job teaching there. And I inherited Benny Powell as a student. Benny studied with me for a couple of years. We got to be really good friends. We don’t see each other a lot now, but we are good friends. We know each other and we enjoy each other. And Benny in those days was studying bass trombone with me, yes. He could play the low notes and he did all the exercises and he got himself into a good player. And I like Benny a lot.
